label: Integrate claude code into ci cd pipelines
model: claude-opus-5 (authored in a Claude Code session)

cards.front: Which four capabilities make Claude Code usable in CI/CD?
cards.back: `-p` (--print) for non-interactive prompt execution, `--output-format json` for machine-readable output, `--json-schema` for enforcing a structured response shape, and stateless session isolation that prevents context leakage between pipeline runs.

cards.front: What does `-p` do, and how does it compose with shell tooling?
cards.back: It passes the prompt on the command line, runs once, and exits — no REPL, no user input. It exits non-zero on failure so pipeline steps can gate on it, and it reads stdin, so you can pipe context in: `git diff HEAD~1 | claude -p "Summarize this diff..."`.

cards.front: Why is stateless session isolation the CORRECT default in a pipeline?
cards.back: Every `claude -p` invocation is independent — no persistent session, no memory of prior runs, no shared context between jobs. That prevents stale context from one PR contaminating another and makes runs reproducible. For multi-turn work, chain explicitly by passing prior output as input, or use --continue / --resume <id>.

cards.front: What does `--output-format json` guarantee, and what does it NOT?
cards.back: It wraps the response in a JSON envelope (result/content, session id, metadata, total_cost_usd) so scripts can parse it with jq. It does NOT constrain the content's shape — add `--json-schema` when downstream code expects specific typed fields. The structured value then lands in the `structured_output` field.

cards.front: Exam trap: you pipe Claude's default output to jq and it fails. Why?
cards.back: Without `--output-format json`, Claude writes conversational prose to stdout — there's nothing for jq to parse. Always pair `--output-format json` with any downstream JSON parsing.

cards.front: Why must CI steps check Claude Code's exit code?
cards.back: It exits 0 on success and non-zero on failure — API errors, rate limits, schema validation failures, missing auth. Without checking (or `set -e`), the step silently continues with empty output. SIGTERM gives exit code 143.

cards.front: How should the API key reach a CI job?
cards.back: Stored as a CI/GitHub secret and injected as an environment variable (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}) — never hardcoded in YAML or scripts. For GitHub Actions you can alternatively use CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from `claude setup-token`, but prefer an API key for org-wide use since the OAuth token is tied to one person's subscription.

cards.front: What does `--bare` do, and why does it matter for scripted runs?
cards.back: It skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills*, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md — cutting startup time and giving the same result on every machine. Without it, a `-p` session loads the same context an interactive one would and will run project hooks and connect .mcp.json servers even in an untrusted folder (no trust dialog in -p). (*It still loads .claude/skills/.)

cards.front: What are the two ways to interact with the GitHub Action, and where do results go?
cards.back: Interactive — mention `@claude` in an issue or PR comment. Automation — supply a `prompt` input so it runs without a mention (on push, pull_request, or schedule). Results go to the workflow run log by default; Claude posts a comment only when the prompt directs it and it has a posting tool.

cards.front: Why can a push made by the action fail to trigger downstream workflows?
cards.back: GitHub does not trigger workflows on commits made with the default GITHUB_TOKEN. Omit the `github_token` input so the action authenticates as the Claude GitHub App (whose pushes do trigger workflows), or pass a custom app token. Note the action also needs `id-token: write` permission for its default GitHub App auth.
